\chapter{Exactly, Really, Nothing}

\hlchaptermodality{95}

\begin{chapteropening}
\textbf{By the end of this chapter:} \emph{I can say exactly, ask really?, answer nothing and not yet, and say the same one.}

\section[cariyāka]{\ta{சரியாக} (cariyāka) — exactly, correctly}

\label{lesson:TA-C95-exactly}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Tamil for one more time, then the Tamil for what did you say.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ta{சரியாக}}
\textbf{\ta{சரியாக}} (\emph{cariyāka}) — \textquotedblleft{}exactly, correctly\textquotedblright{}.

It is the \textbf{\ta{சரி}} of \textquotedblleft{}okay\textquotedblright{}, with \textbf{-\ta{ஆக}}. \textbf{\ta{சரியாகச்} \ta{சொன்னீர்கள்}} — \textquotedblleft{}you said it exactly\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
Okay, made into exactly.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{cariyāka}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{cariyāka}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} say \emph{cariyāka!}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Tamil for one more time, then the Tamil for what did you say, then say \emph{cariyāka} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ta{சரியாக} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}Exactly, correctly\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[uṇmaiyā?]{\ta{உண்மையா}? (uṇmaiyā?) — really? is it true?}

\label{lesson:TA-C95-really}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Tamil for what did you say, then the Tamil for exactly.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ta{உண்மையா}?}
\textbf{\ta{உண்மையா}?} (\emph{uṇmaiyā?}) — \textquotedblleft{}really?\textquotedblright{}, literally \textquotedblleft{}is it the truth?\textquotedblright{}.

\textbf{\ta{உண்மை}} is \textquotedblleft{}truth\textquotedblright{}, and \textbf{-\ta{ஆ}} makes the question.

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
A way to show surprise.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{uṇmaiyā?}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{uṇmaiyā?}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} ask \emph{uṇmaiyā?}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Tamil for what did you say, then the Tamil for exactly, then say \emph{uṇmaiyā?} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ta{உண்மையா}? mean? (\textquotedblleft{}Really? is it true?\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[oṉṟumillai]{\ta{ஒன்றுமில்லை} (oṉṟumillai) — nothing, it's nothing}

\label{lesson:TA-C95-nothing}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Tamil for exactly, then the Tamil for really.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ta{ஒன்றுமில்லை}}
\textbf{\ta{ஒன்றுமில்லை}} (\emph{oṉṟumillai}) — \textquotedblleft{}nothing\textquotedblright{}, \textquotedblleft{}it's nothing\textquotedblright{}.

\textbf{\ta{ஒன்று}} is \textquotedblleft{}one\textquotedblright{}, and \textbf{\ta{இல்லை}} is \textquotedblleft{}no\textquotedblright{}: \emph{not even one}.

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
An answer that closes a question kindly.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{oṉṟumillai}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{oṉṟumillai}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} say \emph{oṉṟumillai}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Tamil for exactly, then the Tamil for really, then say \emph{oṉṟumillai} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ta{ஒன்றுமில்லை} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}Nothing, it's nothing\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[iṉṉum illai]{\ta{இன்னும்} \ta{இல்லை} (iṉṉum illai) — not yet}

\label{lesson:TA-C95-notyet}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Tamil for really, then the Tamil for nothing.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ta{இன்னும்} \ta{இல்லை}}
\textbf{\ta{இன்னும்} \ta{இல்லை}} (\emph{iṉṉum illai}) — \textquotedblleft{}not yet\textquotedblright{}.

\textbf{\ta{இன்னும்}} is \textquotedblleft{}still\textquotedblright{}; with \textbf{\ta{இல்லை}}, \textquotedblleft{}still no\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
Not yet.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{iṉṉum illai}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{iṉṉum illai}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} say \emph{iṉṉum illai}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Tamil for really, then the Tamil for nothing, then say \emph{iṉṉum illai} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ta{இன்னும்} \ta{இல்லை} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}Not yet\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[atē]{\ta{அதே} (atē) — the same, that very one}

\label{lesson:TA-C95-same}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Tamil for nothing, then the Tamil for not yet.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ta{அதே}}
\textbf{\ta{அதே}} (\emph{atē}) — \textquotedblleft{}the same\textquotedblright{}, \textquotedblleft{}that very one\textquotedblright{}.

It is \textbf{\ta{அது}}, \textquotedblleft{}that\textquotedblright{}, with \textbf{-\ta{ஏ}}, \textquotedblleft{}exactly\textquotedblright{}. When someone names what you meant: \textbf{\ta{அதே}!}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
Exactly, really, nothing, not yet, the same.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{atē}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{atē}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} say \emph{atē!}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Tamil for nothing, then the Tamil for not yet, then say \emph{atē} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ta{அதே} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}The same, that very one\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
